claims.text: High-entropy alloys contain multiple principal alloying elements.
The relevant high-entropy alloys have near-equimolar compositions.
The relevant high-entropy alloys exhibit significant atomic-scale chemical disorder.
Such high-entropy alloys are typically used in thermal-insulation applications.

A hybrid model combining ab initio vibrational calculations with machine learning trained on simulated and experimental data will predict low phonon thermal conductivity more accurately than conventional perturbative or effective-medium methods.
Ab initio computations can supply phonon density-of-states data and scattering rates for the hybrid model.
Moderate-to-high temperature regimes relevant to insulation are regimes in which phonon scattering dominates heat transport in the targeted HEAs.
Atomic-scale compositional disorder alters local vibrational modes.
Atomic-scale compositional disorder enhances multiscale phonon scattering.
Ab initio calculations provide precise local vibrational properties and scattering metrics that reveal the effects of disorder on phonon behavior.
Machine learning can use ab initio-derived vibrational and scattering features to generalize thermal-conductivity predictions across complex compositional spaces.
Conventional perturbative and effective-medium models inadequately capture nonlinear, disorder-induced phonon scattering in HEAs.
The hybrid model will reduce phonon-thermal-conductivity prediction error by more than 30% relative to conventional models.
The predicted improvement is limited to HEAs with moderate atomic-scale disorder.
The predicted improvement may not hold in alloys with extreme short-range order.
The predicted improvement may not hold under extreme temperature gradients that induce additional nonlinear effects.
Time-domain thermoreflectance is an established method suitable for measuring the phonon thermal conductivity required by the proposed HEA benchmark.
